gloss: in the end; after all is said and done

definitions.gloss: in the end; after all; when all is said and done; ultimately
definitions.explanation: An expression used to sum up a situation or state a final conclusion after considering various factors. Slightly more emphatic or deliberate than plain {結局|けっきょく}, signaling that the speaker has weighed the matter carefully.

examples.japanese: {結局|けっきょく}のところ、{誰|だれ}も{来|こ}なかった。
{結局|けっきょく}のところ、{何|なに}が{言|い}いたいの？
examples.english: What are you trying to say, when it comes down to it?

examples.japanese: {色々|いろいろ}{検討|けんとう}したが、{結局|けっきょく}のところ{最初|さいしょ}の{案|あん}が{一番|いちばん}よかった。
examples.english: After considering various options, the first proposal turned out to be the best after all.

notes:
An extended form of {結局|けっきょく} (in the end). Adding のところ gives a slightly more reflective, summing-up tone — the speaker is stepping back to give a final assessment.

FORMS:
{結局|けっきょく} + のところ. Can also be written as {結局|けっきょく}の{所|ところ} with kanji.

USAGE:
Typically placed at the beginning of a clause or sentence. Interchangeable with plain {結局|けっきょく} in most contexts, but sounds slightly more measured or formal.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {結局|けっきょく}: in the end (most common, neutral)
- {結局|けっきょく}のところ: when all is said and done (slightly more deliberate)
- つまり: in short, that is to say
- {要|よう}するに: in other words, to put it simply
